reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports L12 precipitation in the fcc phase of Al0.7CoCrFeNi after low-temperature annealing and the associated Orowan strengthening, but all mechanical testing was performed at room temperature under quasi-static and dynamic loading, with no high-temperature data provided. The hypothesis extrapolates this to ~800°C without direct evidence, and the claim of preserved ductility is only partially supported by the truncated text.
premises: Low-temperature annealing of Al0.7CoCrFeNi induces L12 precipitates in the fcc phase
These L12 precipitates are coherent and nano-scale
The precipitates increase yield strength via Orowan bypass
The strengthening occurs without compromising ductility
The alloy system is suitable for high-temperature (~800°C) applications
